d: Pathways resulting in local IgE production in CRSwNP. In the first part, dendritic cells of the skin and mucosa process aeroallergens deposited on the mucosa, and subsequently they present antigens to T cells. T helper 2 cells release their mediators upon recognition of antigens presented by antigen-presenting cells. The Th2 cytokines IL4, IL13, and CD40L induce selective somatic recombination of immunoglobulin heavy chain regions in B cells before maturation into IgE-producing plasma cells. IL5 stimulates eosinophil growth and differentiation. Alternatively, IgE is produced by stimulating innate lymphoid cells to release IL4, IL5, and IL13.

c: Branching interconnected basaloid cell strands, Fibroepithelioma of pinkus, Histopathology slide, Richly vascularised fibrous stroma, histopathology
d:
Fibroepithelioma of Pinkus is characterised by interconnected, branching strands of basaloid cells embedded by a loose, richly vascularised fibrous stroma, extending from the epidermis down into the dermis.
Peripheral nuclear palisading with a formation of follicular germ-like structures can be present. Rarely, isthmic differentiation is present. Fibrotic stroma that can differentiate towards follicular papillae in the areas of germ-like structure formation.

d: A 66 year old diagnosed with Cronkhite-Canada syndrome initially presented with diarrhoea, alopecia and dystrophy of his nails. He described dysgeusia and had a significant recent weight loss. b: Cutaneous mucormycosis: hand in leukaemia patient.
c: Cutaneous mucormycosis, Dorsal hand, Erythema, Fungal hyphae, Fungal infection, Haematoma, Hand, Histopathology-confirmed, Immunocompromised, Rhizopus species cutaneous infection, Staphylococcus epidermidis, Swelling, Therapy-resistant acute myeloid leukaemia, Zygomycosis, infection, Erythematous, vascular disorder, histopathology, systemic condition, hand, lymphatic disorder, male
d:
Rhizopus mucormycosis in a 78-year old presenting with a 3 day history of swelling, erythema and
pain of the dorsal hand, accompanied by a progressing hematoma between the third and fourth finger joints, following a minor laceration when 
gardening.  The fungal infection was treated with serial radical debridements, vacuum-assisted
negative-pressure wound closure technique and intravenous antifungals. Despite successful eradication of the fungal infection, a palliative open wound care concept was implemented during the terminal course of the patient's leukaemia.
f: © Maleitzke T, Elsevier Trauma Case Reports
h:
Maleitzke T, Stahnke K, Trampuz A, Märdian S.
A case report of cutaneous mucormycosis of the hand after minor trauma in a patient with acute myeloid leukaemia.
Trauma Case Reports. 2019:23;100221. doi: 10.1016/j.tcr.2019.100221.

b: Cutaneous mucormycosis: chest wall in skin of colour.
c: Asian ethnicity, Black crust formation, Chest wall, Cutaneous mucormycosis, Fungal hyphae, Fungal infection, Histopathology-confirmed, Male, Necrotic ulcers, Nodules, Red plaques, Rhizopus microsporus, Sensitive-image, Skin of colour, Trunk, Yellow purulent effusion, Zygomycosis, skin of colour, Black, Crust, Chest, infection, histopathology, Necrotic, Ulcer, Nodule, Plaque, Red, Yellow
d: 37-year-old man presenting with large areas of red plaques, nodules, and necrotic ulcers effusing yellow purulent discharge, combined with black crust on the surface and swelling on the rim. The lesion had been present for 17 years initially a 'thumb-size' tender purple patch. It gradually enlarged, to include the whole left chestwall, swelling and rupturing recurrently emitting a clear yellowish fluid. Despite no history of trauma or primary diseases a diagnosis of cutaneous mucormycosis was made based on the history, physical examination, and laboratory results. There was no severe internal organ involvement and patient was treated with oral posaconazole for 150 days with a satisfactory result.
h: Wang Y, Zhu M, Bao Y, Li L, Zhu L, Li F, Xu J, Liang J. Cutaneous mucormycosis caused by Rhizopus microsporus in an immunocompetent patient: a case report and review of literature. Medicine (Baltimore). 2018;97(25):e11141. doi: 10.1097/MD.0000000000011141. PMID: 29924015; PMCID: PMC6024029.

b: The rash of Dengue - fever and severe body and backache started 5 days ago.  There is confluent erythema with white islands ('white in a sea of red')
c: DENV infection, Aedes mosquitoes, Breakbone fever, Confluent erythematosus rash, Dengue virus, Islands of sparing, Leg, Male, Mosquito-borne viral illness, Skin of colour, White islands, infection, environmental and external factors, rash, Sparing, Dermatoscope/dermoscopy
d: Dengue fever rash with typical "island of white in a sea of red". Patient began with a fever, headache and generalised body aches 7-10 days prior to rash. General practitioner treated the symptoms The rash appeared on the 5 -7th day. When seen by a dermatologist the rash had appeared 2 days previously. At this point his fever and headaches had subsided but still had generalised body weakness and complained of mild numbness on thighs and legs. The rash was only on his thighs and legs and was asymptomatic. There was no spontaneous bleeding, peteche, purpura or any other systemic complaint. The patient's platelet count on previous reports were gradually decreasing but was still above 1 lakh but below 150 lakh. He was positive for the IgM antibody for Dengue. The NS1 antigen was negative as he had passed the acute inital phase and was already positive for IgM antibody.

c: Chicken-wire pattern, Direct immune fluorescent test, Direct immunofluorescence, Histopathology slide, Histopathology-image, Dermatoscope/dermoscopy, histopathology
d: Direct immunofluorescence of perilesional skin typically shows staining for IgG, and in most cases C3, against the cell surface of keratinocytes in a characteristic “chicken-wire” pattern. b: Suprabasal intraepidermal blister formation with acantholytic keratinocytes and "tombstone" basal keratinoytes in pemphigus vulgaris
c: Histopathology slide, Histopathology-image, Tombstone pattern, histopathology, Dermatoscope/dermoscopy
d: Pemphigus vulgaris is an intraepidermal vesicular dermatitis. In established lesions there is suprabasilar acantholysis – the basal keratinocytes separate from one another however remain attached to the dermal floor of the blister and resemble “tombstones”. The acantholysis often extends down adjacent hair follicles. Within the superficial dermis, there is typically a superficial perivascular lymphoid infiltrate with occasional eosinophils.

c: 43 years, Environmental and external factors, Female, Forearm, Horse anesthetic, Injecting drug user, Necrotic ulcer, Philly dope, Red painful ulcers, Rhinoceros tranquilizer, Sensitive-image, Skin of colour, Sleep-cut, Surrounding hyperpigmentation, Tranq, Tranq dope, Xylazine-induced ulcers, Zombie drug, arm, Necrotic, Ulcer
d: A 43-year-old woman with a past medical history of severe opioid use disorder and stimulant use disorder presented for wound care. She had multiple ulcerations diffusely over her bilateral forearms with surrounding erythema and warmth. Seven weeks later, she presented to clinic again for wound care because her wounds had progressed.  The wounds started as closed areas of hypopigmentation, then gradually opening, and producing foul-smelling yellow drainage.
